scope: Adversarial integrity bypass paths: TRUNCATE bypass, raw DROP, FK enforcement divergence SQLite vs MySQL, BIGINT overflow, trigger evasion, soft-delete race conditions
method: Read-only adversarial: what would a hostile insider OR a buggy deploy do that the existing immutability layer DOES NOT catch? Cross-reference fiscal triggers (audit_logs/z_reports/cash_movements/stock_movements) against the actual DELETE/UPDATE/TRUNCATE attack surface.

findings.title: TRUNCATE TABLE bypasses ALL MySQL triggers — DDL not DML, immutability defeated
findings.evidence_excerpt: TRUNCATE TABLE stock_movements bypasses MySQL triggers — mitigation = REVOKE TRUNCATE on prod DB user (deploy doc scope, not migration).
findings.impact: MySQL TRUNCATE is DDL — BEFORE DELETE / BEFORE UPDATE triggers do NOT fire. A DBA, deploy script, or compromised app user with TRUNCATE permission can erase: audit_logs (6-year NF525 retention), z_reports (fiscal closure evidence), cash_movements (cash audit), stock_movements (stock audit), order_payments (multi-tender breakdown). PRISON-TIME consequence if a tax inspection finds a TRUNCATE event in the binlog (and a binlog event for TRUNCATE IS recorded, FYI — but recovery from binlog is non-trivial). BRAIN explicitly flags this as 'owner-deferred' — but post 7/7 GO V1 LOCAL state and given the deploy is imminent, this remains the single most catastrophic integrity gap.
findings.mitigation_present: (a) BRAIN deploy doc says REVOKE TRUNCATE on prod DB user — owner-deferred. (b) MySQL binlog records the TRUNCATE event (forensic recovery possible but slow). (c) FreshOrderSeed command does NOT touch fiscal tables (only orders+order_items).
findings.recommendation: P0 BLOCKER for production migrate. Before V1 ship: (1) Verify DB GRANT in deploy doc (owner gate). (2) Add CI gate: `mysql -e "SHOW GRANTS FOR 'app_user'"` MUST NOT include TRUNCATE on tables: audit_logs, z_reports, cash_movements, stock_movements, order_payments, orders, order_items. (3) Document in PROJECT_BRAIN.md §8 NF525 Fiscal Invariants. (4) Optional belt-and-braces: MySQL 8.0+ supports DEFINER triggers on TRUNCATE-impossible CHECK constraints — but no real way to disallow TRUNCATE via DDL. The GRANT is the only defence.

findings.title: SQLite FK enforcement OFF by default — production runs MySQL but tests run SQLite, FK violations invisible in test suite
findings.impact: Default IS true (good), so PHPUnit RefreshDatabase enables FK. BUT 5+ migration files and seeders explicitly `PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF` then ON in their up() (2026_05_05_000020, 2026_05_16_140100, 2026_03_11_000000, MenuSeeder, ItemCategoryService). If an exception breaks between OFF and ON, the test session continues with FK_CHECKS=0 — any subsequent test in the same SQLite memory DB could insert orphan rows. PHPUnit reuses the in-memory DB across tests in a class via RefreshDatabase trait → cross-test contamination potential.
findings.mitigation_present: Most migrations wrap PRAGMA in try/finally or transaction blocks (verified for 2026_05_05_000020). MenuSeeder line 314 enables OFF outside try/catch — possible leak.
findings.recommendation: (1) Audit each PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF site for try/finally wrapping. (2) Add a CI test sentinel that asserts PRAGMA foreign_keys returns 1 at the END of every test class teardown. (3) Refactor seeders to use Eloquent + cascade explicitly instead of disabling FKs.

findings.title: MySQL down() migration drop on z_reports + audit_logs is guarded — but the dropImmutabilityTriggers() helper is called BEFORE the env guard
findings.impact: CORRECT ORDER actually — env guard FIRST (lines 70-76), then drop triggers (line 78), then drop table (lines 80-82). I was checking for the inverse pattern and it's not present here. Good. RED-classifies as a check-and-confirm: the env guard pattern is consistent across audit_logs + z_reports + audit_logs_branch_prev_unique index.
findings.recommendation: No action. RED-team confirmed defence sound. Document this pattern as the canonical NF525 down() template in CLAUDE.md §8.

findings.title: audit_logs immutability triggers can be DROPPED via raw DDL by a DBA — no DDL-protection layer
findings.impact: A DBA with TRIGGER privilege can drop the audit_logs immutability triggers, then UPDATE/DELETE rows freely, then RE-CREATE the triggers (replaying the migration's create block). MySQL binlog records DROP TRIGGER + UPDATE + CREATE TRIGGER — forensic recovery possible. Identical class to RED-001: defence is GRANT-level only.
findings.recommendation: Same as RED-001: REVOKE TRIGGER privilege on prod DB user for tables audit_logs, z_reports, cash_movements, stock_movements. Document in deploy doc. CI gate `SHOW GRANTS` check before V1 ship.

findings.title: fiscal_sequence_no BIGINT overflow — non-issue but task asked: confirmed 9.2 quintillion ceiling
findings.impact: unsignedBigInteger = 0 to 18,446,744,073,709,551,615 (~18.4 quintillion). At 1M orders/day per branch = 50 billion years. Not a real risk. Worth noting because task specifically asked.
findings.recommendation: No action. Document in BRAIN that fiscal_sequence_no is BIGINT and overflow is not a credible threat.

findings.title: Soft-delete RACE: BranchScope filters by deleted_at IS NULL implicitly via SoftDeletes trait — concurrent soft-delete + read could expose deleted row
findings.evidence_path: app/Models/Order.php (uses SoftDeletes trait) + app/Models/Scopes/BranchScope.php (no deleted_at handling)
findings.impact: Adversarial scenario: a kiosk user is checking out, the cashier soft-deletes the order via admin UI between READ and WRITE. The READ returned a non-deleted row (deleted_at=NULL); the kiosk's UPDATE happens after the soft-delete commits. Default MySQL REPEATABLE READ isolation MIGHT save us via snapshot — but only within a transaction. The kiosk path uses idempotency keys + payment locks (FrontendOrderService et al.) which mitigate.
findings.mitigation_present: Idempotency middleware + Cache::lock + SELECT FOR UPDATE in payment-critical paths (FrontendOrderService:1023 reference area).
findings.recommendation: Audit which write paths use SELECT FOR UPDATE on orders. POS finalize/cancel + Kiosk payment-confirm paths verified to use it. Reconcile-pending (PaymentReconcileController:194-247) uses withoutGlobalScope + locking — sound. Document in BRAIN that any new admin write on Order MUST be wrapped in FOR UPDATE if it competes with frontend writes.

findings.title: Order soft-delete + restore-disabled = an order can be 'lost' if the only soft-delete path is OrderService::destroy
findings.impact: Restore is blocked. If an order is accidentally soft-deleted (admin clicked the wrong row), the only recovery is via raw SQL `UPDATE orders SET deleted_at=NULL WHERE id=X`. That bypasses Eloquent so the restore-block doesn't fire, but it ALSO doesn't fire the `restoring`/`restored` events — and ARCH-004 explains that OrderAddress + OrderCoupon were HARD deleted alongside, so the restored Order is permanently broken. Tested deliberate behaviour but the soft-delete UI itself is the threat surface.
findings.mitigation_present: OrderService::destroy() likely has confirmation UI (not verified in this audit).
findings.recommendation: Verify the admin UI requires confirmation for soft-delete. Consider adding a 'reason' field to deletion_log (table exists per 2026_04_15_230200) and surface it in the admin UI. Defensive UI design — out of WI-3 DB scope but flagged.

findings.title: WH-3 anchor: daily_reset_at DATE column + Carbon::today() = TZ mismatch — VERIFIED FIXED in code
findings.impact: WH-3 caught: DATE column vs MySQL session TZ=UTC vs app TZ=Paris. Fix applied: use Carbon::today(config('app.timezone'))->toDateString() to bind a Paris-local Y-m-d. RED-team checks: are there OTHER DATE columns with similar mismatch? Inventory: business_date on orders (DATE), daily_reset_at on item_branch_availability (DATE). Both treated consistently in services post-fix. NO other DATE columns found in active critical paths.
findings.recommendation: No new finding. Confirms WH-3 anchor + sister-services pattern (Carbon::today(tz)) applied consistently.

findings.title: Concurrent fiscal_sequence_no allocation race — Cache::lock(5s) + SELECT FOR UPDATE = triple defence, BUT cache driver downtime risks
findings.evidence_excerpt: Cache::lock 5s + DB FOR UPDATE = triple défense concurrent
findings.impact: If Redis is down, Cache::lock fails. Falls back to DB FOR UPDATE only — still safe but loses one layer. Adversarial scenario: Redis OOM + 100 concurrent kiosk orders = some get gaps in fiscal_sequence_no if FOR UPDATE timeout < transaction time. UNIQUE(branch_id, fiscal_sequence_no) catches obvious duplicates; gaps are silent.
findings.recommendation: No action — defence-in-depth IS the design. Document in monitoring runbook: alert if Redis lock failure rate >0 for >1min. Out of WI-3 scope.

findings.title: stock_movements idempotency_key NULL allows duplicate inserts when caller forgets to populate
findings.impact: UNIQUE on a nullable column: MySQL/SQLite allow multiple NULL rows. If the writer (StockService etc.) forgets to set idempotency_key, the immutability triggers prevent UPDATE/DELETE so a duplicate becomes permanent NF525-grade junk in the audit. RED-team: are there any code paths that insert stock_movements without idempotency_key? Need StockMovement::create or DB::table inserts inspection.
findings.mitigation_present: Service layer populates idempotency_key from event correlation (order_id + reason combo).
findings.recommendation: Audit StockMovement::create call sites for idempotency_key presence. Tighten model layer: add `static::creating(fn($sm) => $sm->idempotency_key ?? throw new InvariantViolation('stock_movements must have idempotency_key'))`. 3-LOC defensive add.

summary.highest_impact_finding: RED-001 (TRUNCATE TABLE bypasses ALL MySQL triggers — fiscal evidence erasable via DDL; GRANT-level defence required at deploy)
summary.next_class_of_finding: RED-002 + RED-004 — DDL-level attack surface (PRAGMA foreign_keys, DROP TRIGGER). Application-layer triggers are necessary but not sufficient; the DB GRANT layer is the closing argument.

adversarial_paths_NOT_finding_issues: audit_logs UPDATE/DELETE via Eloquent: blocked by both model and DB triggers (defence-in-depth confirmed).
z_reports UPDATE/DELETE: same defence shape, blocked.
fiscal_sequence_no monotonic per branch: UNIQUE(branch_id, fiscal_sequence_no) + Cache::lock + FOR UPDATE triple defence. Gap-handling via fiscal_alloc_error_at + retry cron. Sound.
Kiosk Sanctum kiosk:order ability: 6+ controllers check tokenCan() consistently.
BranchScope coverage of 22 models matches BRAIN §9 list.
FK enforcement in MySQL prod: foreign_key_constraints=true default + most cascade chains documented and intentional.
